15357-the-notorious-mrs-ebbsmith.title: The Notorious Mrs. Ebbsmith
15357-the-notorious-mrs-ebbsmith.creator: Arthur Wing Pinero
15357-the-notorious-mrs-ebbsmith.description: A book by Arthur Wing Pinero. (The Signora Thorpe.) NELLO. (With her brother.) ANTONIO. [Calling.] Buon di, Signor Winterfield! [Good day, Signor Winterfield! The blessing of God be upon you!] NELLA. [Calling.] Buon di, Signora! May the Virgin have you in her keeping!) ANTONIO. [Returning to the room.] Noi siamo in ritardo di tutto questa mattina. (We are behindhand with everything this morning.) NELLA. [Following him.] E vero. (That is true.) ANTONIO. [Bustling about.] La stufa! [Throwing wood into the stove.] Che tua sia benedetta per rammentarmelo!

27804-the-boarding-school-familiar-conve.title: The Boarding School Familiar Conversations Between A Governe
27804-the-boarding-school-familiar-conve.creator: Unknown
27804-the-boarding-school-familiar-conve.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Jane smiled, as she said, "Since you are so very doubtful of your abilities, I think I will give a short lesson upon teaching. Suppose you ask your pupil if she has learned grammar: if she replies in the affirmative, desire her to explain the nature of the different parts of speech.

arxiv-2110-08305.title: Universal finite-size amplitude and anomalous entanglement entropy of z = 2 z=2 quantum Lifshitz criticalities in topological chains
arxiv-2110-08305.creator: Ke Wang, T. A. Sedrakyan
arxiv-2110-08305.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ke Wang, T. A. Sedrakyan. We consider Lifshitz criticalities with dynamical exponent z = 2 z=2 that emerge in a class of topological chains. There, such a criticality plays a fundamental role in describing transitions between symmetry-enriched conformal field theories (CFTs). We report that, at such critical points in one spatial dimension, the finite-size correction to the energy scales with system size, L L , as ∼ L − 2 \sim L^{-2} , with universal and anomalously large coefficient.

arxiv-2302-07237.title: Effect of the excitation setup in the improved enhancement factor of covered-gold-nanorod-dimer antennas
arxiv-2302-07237.creator: Iván A. Ramos 1,2 , L. M. León Hilario 1 , María L. Pedano 2, A. A. Reynoso 2,3
arxiv-2302-07237.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Iván A. Ramos 1,2 , L. M. León Hilario 1 , María L. Pedano 2, A. A. Reynoso 2,3. Devices possessing the ability to sense both electrically and optically molecular targets are of fundamental and technological interest. Towards this end, it has been shown that covering the ends of gapped gold-nanorod-dimer nanoantennas can improve the enhancement factor (EF) that quantifies the nanoantenna efficiency for surface-enhancement Raman spectroscopy (SERS) for an incident wave coming from the top of the sample.

arxiv-2306-13698.title: 4K × \times 4K CCD Imager for the 3.6m DOT: Recent up-gradations and results
arxiv-2306-13698.creator: S. B. Pandey 1∗, Amit Kumar 1,2∗∗, B. K. Reddy 1, S. Yadav 1, N. Nanjappa 1, Amar Aryan 1,3, Rahul Gupta 1,3, Neelam Panwar 1, and R. K. S. Yadav 1
arxiv-2306-13698.description: Abstract The 4K × \times 4K CCD Imager is the first light instrument for the 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope and is producing broad-band imaging observations of many Galactic and extra-galactic sources since 2015-2016. Capabilities of the CCD Imager are demonstrated recently through several publications using the well-calibrated multi-band deep photometric results as expected from other similar facilities globally.

arxiv-2308-02085.title: Microscopic Gyration with Dissipative Coupling
arxiv-2308-02085.creator: Soham Dutta, Arnab Saha
arxiv-2308-02085.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Soham Dutta, Arnab Saha. Microscopic gyrators, including (but not limited to) Brownian gyrators (BGs), require anisotropic fluctuations to perform gyration. It produces a finite current, driving the system out of equilibrium. In a typical BG set-up with an isotropic (i.e. spherical) colloidal particle, the anisotropy sets in by the coupling among space dimensions via an externally applied anisotropic (spherically asymmetric) potential confining the particle and the difference between the temperatures along various space dimensions.

arxiv-2411-01067.title: Randomized Controlled Trials for Security Copilot for IT Administrators
arxiv-2411-01067.creator: James Bono, Alec Xu
arxiv-2411-01067.description: Abstract As generative AI (GAI) tools become increasingly integrated into workplace environments, it is essential to measure their impact on productivity across specific domains. This study evaluates the effects of Microsoft’s Security Copilot (“Copilot”) on information technology administrators (“IT admins”) through randomized controlled trials.

arxiv-2501-07742.title: RePoseD: Efficient Relative Pose Estimation With Known Depth Information
arxiv-2501-07742.creator: Yaqing Ding, Viktor Kocur, Václav Vávra, Zuzana Berger Haladová, Jian Yang, Torsten Sattler, Zuzana Kukelova
arxiv-2501-07742.description: Abstract Recent advances in monocular depth estimation methods (MDE) and their improved accuracy open new possibilities for their applications. In this paper, we investigate how monocular depth estimates can be used for relative pose estimation. In particular, we are interested in answering the question whether using MDEs improves results over traditional point-based methods.

arxiv-2505-04646.title: Computational Irreducibility as the Foundation of Agency: A Formal Model Connecting Undecidability to Autonomous Behavior in Complex Systems
arxiv-2505-04646.creator: Poria Azadi
arxiv-2505-04646.description: Abstract This article presents a formal model demonstrating that genuine autonomy, the ability of a system to self-regulate and pursue objectives, fundamentally implies computational unpredictability from an external perspective. We establish precise mathematical connections, proving that for any truly autonomous system, questions about its future behavior are fundamentally undecidable.

arxiv-2506-20364.title: Path-Based Approach for Detecting and Assessing Inconsistency in Network Meta-Analysis: A Novel Method
arxiv-2506-20364.creator: Noosheen R. Tahmasebi, Annabel L. Davies, Theodoros Papakonstantinou, Gerta Rücker, Adriani Nikolakopoulou
arxiv-2506-20364.description: Abstract Network Meta-Analysis (NMA) plays a pivotal role in synthesizing evidence from various sources and comparing multiple interventions. At its core, NMA relies on integrating both direct evidence from head-to-head comparisons and indirect evidence from different paths that link treatments through common comparators. A key aspect is evaluating consistency between direct and indirect sources.

arxiv-2512-09861.title: The Limits of Line Broadening: Modeling Stellar Spectra and Formation Temperatures at High Resolution Julia ( 9 ) , Korg.jl ( 41 ; 42 ) , Matplotlib ( 26 ), JuliaGPU ( 8 )
arxiv-2512-09861.creator: Michael L. Palumbo III
arxiv-2512-09861.description: Abstract The modeling of stellar spectra is pervasive in astronomy. Conventionally, the shapes of absorption lines are modeled by convolving thermal profiles (computed given some model stellar atmosphere and line list) with broadening kernels intended to account for the effects of rotation and other nonthermal sources of broadening (i.e., macroturbulence).

arxiv-2602-10386.title: Colorful Talks with Graphs: Human-Interpretable Graph Encodings for Large Language Models
arxiv-2602-10386.creator: Angelo Zangari, Peyman Baghershahi, Sourav Medya
arxiv-2602-10386.description: Abstract Graph problems are fundamentally challenging for large language models (LLMs). While LLMs excel at processing unstructured text, graph tasks require reasoning over explicit structure, permutation invariance, and computationally complex relationships, creating a mismatch with the representations of text-based models. Our work investigates how LLMs can be effectively applied to graph problems despite these barriers.

arxiv-2603-06322.creator: Dongfen Bian, Shouyi Dai, Emmanuel Grenier

pmc-10777591.title: Combined Facile Synthesis, Purification, and Surface Functionalization Approach Yields Monodispersed Gold Nanorods for Drug Delivery Applications
pmc-10777591.creator: Shunping Han, Khuloud T Al‐Jamal
pmc-10777591.description: Synthesizing gold nanorods (AuNRs) by seed‐mediated growth method results in the presence of undesired size and shape particles by‐products occupying 10–90% of the population. In this study, AuNRs are synthesized by the seed‐mediated growth method using cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) as a surfactant.

pmc-11454163.title: 6369 Weiss-Kruszka Syndrome and Growth Hormone Deficiency, Adrenal Insufficiency, and Morbid Obesity
pmc-11454163.creator: Taimy Falcon-Rodriguez, Natalia Solano, Alejandro Diaz
pmc-11454163.description: Disclosure: T. Falcon-Rodriguez: None. N. Solano: None. A. Diaz: None. Background: Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WKSA) is a rare autosomal dominant genetic disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the ZNF462 gene. Individuals affected by this condition exhibit distinctive craniofacial features, ptosis, dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, hearing loss, intellectual disability, and hypotonia.

pmc-11714544.title: Effects of Self‐Perceptions of Cognitive Decline on Cognitive Assessment Outcomes in the Women’s Alzheimer’s Movement Prevention Center at Cleveland Clinic
pmc-11714544.creator: Nikki L Kaplan, Emily Post, Taylor F Levine, Jessica ZK Caldwell
pmc-11714544.description: BackgroundThe Women’s Alzheimer’s Movement Prevention Center (WAMPC) at Cleveland Clinic evaluates women’s risk factors for developing Alzheimer’s disease and provides personalized recommendations for reducing risk. Previous research has established that up to 40% of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) cases might be prevented when modifiable risk factors are addressed.

pmc-12374299.title: Experiences of kidney transplantation for recipients in regional, rural, and remote Queensland – exploring the trials and tribulations
pmc-12374299.creator: Tara K. Watters, Beverley D. Glass, Nicole J. Scholes-Robertson, Andrew J. Mallett
pmc-12374299.description: BackgroundPeople with kidney failure, unable to access kidney transplantation are disadvantaged in terms of their quality of life and overall survival. Despite this, regional, rural, and remote populations worldwide remain less likely to receive a kidney transplant and often experience unique difficulties throughout their transplant journey.

pmc-12398532.title: Communicating with two vehicles immediately ahead boosts traffic capacity sixfold in connected autonomous vehicle platoons
pmc-12398532.creator: Shi-Teng Zheng, Rui Jiang, Xiqun (Michael) Chen, Junfang Tian, Xiao Han, Ruidong Yan, Bin Jia, Xiaobo Qu, Zhen-Hua Li, Lan-Da Gao, Fang Zhang, De-Zhao Zhang, Ziyou Gao
pmc-12398532.description: Addressing urban congestion through enhanced traffic capacity has emerged as a critical objective for connected autonomous driving technologies. An irredundant communication connectivity topology is essential for ensuring the high efficiency and stability of the traffic system, which has not been fully validated due to the scarcity of real-world tests.

pmc-12564847.title: Mechanism and Application of Developmental Factors in Plant Genetic Transformation
pmc-12564847.creator: Lixin Zhang, Fang Wang, Biao Luo, Na Chen, Yan Wang, Xianwen Zhang
pmc-12564847.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Genetic transformation serves as a critical tool for gene function research and crop improvement. However, its efficiency is often low and highly dependent on species, genotypes, and explant types, significantly restricting its broader application. Many developmental factors have been proven pivotal not only for plant growth and development but also for the regulation of callus formation and shoot regeneration, which are key steps in the process of genetic transformation.

pmc-12776226.title: Machine learning screening for disulfidptosis genes-associated immunosuppression status in osteosarcoma and rhabdomyosarcoma
pmc-12776226.creator: Lin Yu, Fanli Lin
pmc-12776226.description: BackgroundThe recent identification of disulfidptosis, a novel form of cell death, offers significant potential for advancing cancer therapeutics. Osteosarcoma (OS) and rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) are prevalent malignant sarcomas in children and young adults, yet their molecular underpinnings remain poorly understood, hampering treatment options.

pmc-12784524.title: Epstein-Barr virus infection shapes the genetic, transcriptomic, and immune microenvironment landscape of Burkitt lymphoma
pmc-12784524.creator: Qing Xiao, Yilei Zhang, Zhongyi Chen, Xinrong Liu, Wentao Yu, Tiansheng Wang, Ling Chu
pmc-12784524.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Burkitt lymphoma (BL) is a highly aggressive B-cell lymphoma with its occurrence and progression closely associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) status. However, the molecular differences between EBV-positive and EBV-negative BL have not been comprehensively evaluated. Through targeted sequencing of a 475-gene panel in 27 BL cases, and RNA-seq and LncRNA-seq analyses of 25 cases, we found that EBV-negative tumors displayed a higher frequency of chromosomal amplifications, particularly at 7p12.2, 6q25.3 and 7q22.1.

pmc-13092480.title: Octopus sucker-inspired, Turkish gall extract-integrated microneedle patch for oral ulcer mitigation
pmc-13092480.creator: Lin Lin, Shilin Guo, Cheng Zhao, Xiaotan Dou, Wei Han, Chuanhui Song
pmc-13092480.description: SummaryDespite pharmacological advancements of oral ulcer treatment, developing sustained-release delivery systems remains a challenge. To address this, we designed a bioinspired microneedle platform integrating Turkish gall extract for targeted ulcer therapy. Drawing on the structural principles of octopus suckers, we fabricated a 3D-printed microneedle array with suction-enhanced morphology, replicated into a hydrogel-based mold.

pmc-13176315.title: Presence of bacterial DNA in synovial fluid from the temporomandibular joint in patients with temporomandibular joint disorders
pmc-13176315.creator: Nikoo Bazsefidpay, Mattias Ulmner, Anastasios Damdimopoulos, Bodil Lund
pmc-13176315.description: IntroductionTemporomandibular joint disorders (TMJD) are common, affecting approximately 30% of the population. While the aetiology of TMJD has been considerably discussed, one aspect that has not been thoroughly investigated is the potential occurrence and role of bacteria in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). This study aimed to determine the existence of bacteria in the TMJ synovial fluid of patients with TMJD.

pmc-13314076.title: Anticancer and immune effect of the extracted brown Raoultella planticola pigment on murine mammary adenocarcinoma (AMN3)
pmc-13314076.creator: Karrar Ali Mohammed Hasan Alsakini, Asmaa Hamoody Abdullah, Hind H. Al-Ammiri
pmc-13314076.description: Background: Raoultella planticola is a developing pathogen that can infect both humans and animals. Raoultella spp. commonly colonize the gastrointestinal and upper respiratory systems. It usually causes pneumonia, bile tract infections, and bacteremia.Aim:In this study, the anticancer activity of an isolated brown pigment of a R. planticola isolate was tested in vitro.

pmc-13385782.title: Sad emotion processing-related theta oscillation patterns link suicide attempt to childhood trauma in depression: evidence from MEG
pmc-13385782.creator: Yi Xia, Yishan Du, Moxuan Song, Junling Sheng, Rui Yan, Xiaoqin Wang, Zhijian Yao, Qing Lu
pmc-13385782.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a severe mood disorder with genetic and environmental interactions. Subtypes with childhood trauma (CT) tend to have higher rates of suicide attempt (SA). The amygdala (AMY) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) are integral to the neurocircuitry underlying emotional processing, with dysregulation of these regions being posited as a pathophysiological hallmark both in CT and SA.

pmc-13435652.title: Brain-wide spatiotemporal mapping of glutamate/GABA dual-transmitter neurons during postnatal development in mice
pmc-13435652.creator: Cong Zhou, Shihan Cheng, Haofu Zheng, Xiaochuan Zou, Yihui Bi, Hongsheng Wang
pmc-13435652.description: Emerging evidence suggests that individual neurons can utilize multiple neurotransmitters, challenging traditional views of neuronal identity. However, as most studies to date have focused on the adult stage, a fundamental question remains: does this dual-transmitter phenotype emerge only in adulthood, or does it have specific developmental origins?

pmc-13441897.title: Ethanolamine as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for depressive disorder
pmc-13441897.creator: Shintaro Ogawa, Kotaro Hattori, Shinsuke Hidese, Daimei Sasayama, Miho Ota, Tomoko Miyakawa, Megumi Tatsumi, Ryo Matsumura, Sumiko Yoshida, Takamasa Noda, Minoru Takebayashi, Wataru Omori, Kei Itagaki, Naoto Kajitani, Mami Okada-Tsuchioka, Akitoyo Hishimoto, Shuken Boku, Tadasu Horai, Akira Monji, Y
pmc-13441897.description: We investigated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) ethanolamine (EA) levels in major depressive disorder (MDD), to validate our previous findings on EA (Ogawa et al., 2015) and broaden its biological context and translational relevance. Using human samples (sets A–C) and animal models, we explored the implications for replication, translational potential, therapeutic development, and mechanistic insight.

pmc-13540017.title: Percentage of Low-Attenuation Epicardial Adipose Volume (LAAV%) as an Independent Predictor of Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13540017.creator: Hui Ding, Linlin Sun, Shuangxiang Lin, Xincheng Li, Haipeng Liu, Zhen Wang
pmc-13540017.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Clinically, coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) remains a significant diagnostic challenge because the associated symptoms frequently overlap with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). This condition may contribute to cardiac ischemic events regardless of the presence of obstructive epicardial lesions.

pmc-13609464.title: Structural Characterization of Ettringite Synthesized in the Presence of Arsenate(V) and Chromate(VI) Ions
pmc-13609464.creator: Magdalena Król, Witold Jastrzębski, Włodzimierz Mozgawa
pmc-13609464.description: Ettringite (Ca6[Al(OH)6]2(SO4)3⋅26H2O) is an important hydration product involved in the immobilization of oxyanion contaminants in cementitious systems; however, the structural effects of arsenate(V) and chromate(VI) incorporation remain poorly understood. This study investigates the influence of both oxyanions on the formation and structure of ettringite-based materials using X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Rietveld refinement and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR).
